title: Find the most frequent words in real speeches
description:
Write a function `most_frequent_words_in_file(path, n)` that reads the text file at `path` and returns the `n` most frequent words (case-insensitive) as `(count, word)` tuples.

Covers source items 3 (ten most frequent words in each of 4 real speeches) and 5 (ten most repeated words in Romeo and Juliet) as one exercise with 5 test cases - both ask for the same operation on a different file.
starter_code:
import re
from collections import Counter


def most_frequent_words_in_file(path, n):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: Idea to consider: read the file, then reuse the same tokenize-and-count approach as find_most_common_words
The only difference from counting words in a string directly is one extra step at the start - reading the file's contents into a string first.
Open and read the file, tokenize with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text.lower()), count with Counter, and return the top n sorted by (-count, word).
expected_behavior: Returns the n most frequent words in the file, most frequent first.
solution:
import re
from collections import Counter


def most_frequent_words_in_file(path, n):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text.lower())
    counts = Counter(words)
    ranked = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
    return [(count, word) for word, count in ranked[:n]]
explanation: The most common words in ordinary English text are overwhelmingly function words ('the', 'and', 'to') regardless of speaker or subject - the same top few dominate every one of these five very different texts.
